key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 strongly tunes bandgap and photovoltaic performance, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the best solar-cell candidate.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests composition engineering can optimize perovskite absorbers for higher efficiency and better material selection in optoelectronic device design.
method: First-principles calculations of structural, electronic, and optical properties.
Band-structure analysis to determine bandgap type and magnitude.
SLME-based screening to estimate photovoltaic efficiency.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps of 2.0–3.788 eV across the series and a peak SLME of 29.6% for Ca3PI3 versus 0.6% for Ca3PF3.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on computational screening, so experimental stability, defect tolerance, and device fabrication effects still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
